text.p: These are the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central Bank cuts interest rates. Bankers say the move will help reactivate the economy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says unity between Jordanians and Palestinians in Jordan does not mean that Palestinians should be deprived of their rights in Palestine.
- Tawfiq Fakhouri, Bank of Jordan chairman, denies he planned to take control of Jordan Kuwait Bank.
- Jordan Valley authorities working on 9.5 million dinar ($13.4 million) project to improve King Abdallah irrigation canal.

- Islamist sources say Moslem Brotherhood executive council will call a meeting of the organisation's consultative council within days to take final decision on whether to boycott parliamentary elections.
- Leila Feisal, sister of Jordan's only woman MP Toujan Feisal, says she will stand for parliament too.
- Ad-Dustour learns that the Christian Democratic party, which has applied for permission to be formally established, is a religious-based party, contradicting Jordan's law on political parties.
- Consumer group criticises increase in doctors' medical charges.
- Deputy Prime Minister Jawad al-Anani says Jordan is getting more foreign investment, but it would prefer Arab investment.
- Royal Jordanian airlines to resume flights to Kuwait on Thursday.
- Jordan Kuwait Bank general assembly meetings cancelled over irregularities.
